summary:
Field Shift: A Data-Driven Crop Rotation & Decision Support Assistant

In semi-arid regions like the Konya Plain, farmers often struggle with crop rotation decisions due to severe water deficits, unpredictable climates, and varying soil types. Traditional trial-and-error methods or generalized advice frequently lead to suboptimal yields, water depletion, and economic loss.

To address this challenge, we developed Field Shift, an interactive web-based decision support assistant. By integrating 20 years of historical climate records from the NASA POWER Daily API with peer-reviewed local agronomic trials and FAO-56 crop water demand models, our platform provides evidence-based, parcel-level crop rotation comparisons. Farmers input their specific coordinates, soil group, previous crops, and primary goals (e.g., water conservation or economic margin). Instead of prescribing a single "miracle crop," Field Shift displays transparent, multi-year scenarios (such as wheat-fallow vs. wheat-chickpea) along with their documented strengths and environmental risks.

This solution is crucial because it bridges the gap between complex satellite data and practical farming. By empowering farmers with understandable, localized, and scientifically backed insights, Field Shift promotes sustainable water management, enhances soil health, and helps secure agricultural livelihoods in vulnerable ecosystems.
details:
Our project is an interactive map application that visualizes environmental and climatic changes across agricultural lands in the Konya basin. It enables users to examine land-use changes and the impacts of drought in the region through a timeline.

How it Works and Benefits: Through an HTML and JavaScript-based map interface, users can toggle different satellite data layers on and off. Visualizing the depletion of water resources and the stress on agricultural areas serves as an early warning system for both local farmers and policymakers.

Tools Used: The application was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, utilizing the Leaflet.js library and OpenStreetMap data for the mapping infrastructure. We used GitHub for version control and deployment, and received support from generative AI tools (Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude) during the data analysis and coding processes.
